negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence of a public reference does not mean absence of a deal — these vendors sell into CEE and may be under NDA or announce only via partner channels. The vendor pages should remain on the monitoring list rather than being written off.

brief: For Slovenia, the global platform vendors do publish their wins, but sparsely: the one strong confirmed anchor is Temenos, whose success-story and newsroom pages name NLB (core upgrade to T24/UniversalSuite R17, retail migration following N Banka) — corroborated independently by FinTech Futures, which also names the SI payments-infrastructure deal between Bankart and Nets. Backbase, Mambu, Finastra, Thought Machine, Finacle and FLEXCUBE surfaced no SI-named reference in this pass and should be treated as monitoring targets, not as evidence of absence. The richer, denser layer is local: HRC (Hibis) names Addiko, Delavska hranilnica and Gorenjska banka as clients, SETCCE enumerates NLB, Sparkasse, Gorenjska banka and Delavska hranilnica in Slovene, and Halcom's bank listings map the corporate e-banking channel bank-by-bank — these local vendor reference pages are the best available public stack map of the SI market. Two indirect channels round it out: buyer-side newsrooms (NLB Group, OTP banka's merger IT-migration releases) that date and validate vendor claims, and Slovene press on failed migrations (BKS Bank) that exposes core replacements no vendor advertises.
